questiontext.text:
Two linear relations are given:

Relation A \[ y={@m1@}x+({@c1@}) \]

Relation B \[ y={@m2@}x+({@c2@}) \]

Plot both relations on the Cartesian plane.

Move points \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) to create Relation A. Move points \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) to create Relation B.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="sA1" input-ref-ans2="sA2" input-ref-ans3="sB1" input-ref-ans4="sB2"]] JXG.Options.text.useMathJax = true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard( divid, { axis: true, showCopyright: false, boundingbox: [-6,6,6,-6], keepaspectratio: true, grid: true } ); var a1 = board.create( 'point', [{#start_ax1#},{#start_ay1#}], { name:'A1', snapToGrid:true, size:3, snapSizeX:0.1, snapSizeY:0.1, showInfobox:false } ); var a2 = board.create( 'point', [{#start_ax2#},{#start_ay2#}], { name:'A2', snapToGrid:true, size:3, snapSizeX:0.1, snapSizeY:0.1, showInfobox:false } ); var lineA = board.create( 'line', [a1,a2], { fixed:true, straightFirst:true, straightLast:true, strokeWidth:2 } ); var b1 = board.create( 'point', [{#start_bx1#},{#start_by1#}], { name:'B1', snapToGrid:true, size:3, snapSizeX:0.1, snapSizeY:0.1, showInfobox:false } ); var b2 = board.create( 'point', [{#start_bx2#},{#start_by2#}], { name:'B2', snapToGrid:true, size:3, snapSizeX:0.1, snapSizeY:0.1, showInfobox:false } ); var lineB = board.create( 'line', [b1,b2], { fixed:true, straightFirst:true, straightLast:true, strokeWidth:2, dash:2 } ); stack_jxg.bind_point( sA1, a1 ); stack_jxg.bind_point( sA2, a2 ); stack_jxg.bind_point( sB1, b1 ); stack_jxg.bind_point( sB2, b2 ); board.unsuspendUpdate(); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

For a line \[ y=mx+c, \] one convenient point is its \(y\)-intercept: \[ (0,c). \]

For Relation A, \[ y={@m1@}x+({@c1@}), \] two points are \[ (0,{@c1@}) \] and \[ (1,{@m1+c1@}). \]

For Relation B, \[ y={@m2@}x+({@c2@}), \] two points are \[ (0,{@c2@}) \] and \[ (1,{@m2+c2@}). \]

Any two distinct points lying on the correct relation define the same straight line, so your points do not have to match these example points.
